articleTitle: Target Tracking With The Hough Transform
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: The Hough transform is a convenient and efficient means for detecting and tracking point targets that move in straight lines in video or cinematic imagery. The Hough technique converts collinear points in se quential frames of video or cinematic imagery to a delta function in the transform space. Moving targets are detected by looking for delta functions with a threshold operator. The slope and intercept of the target trajectory are inferred from the transform-space coordinates of the detected delta functions.

articleTitle: Executable Assertions - An Aid To Reliable Software
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: Two preprocessors, one for and one for have been implemented to allow "executable assertions" to be added to the source code. These assertions make it possible to carry out certain static and dynamic checks on the semantics of a program. They can detect errors in input data and prevent error propagation. It is possible to in clude remedial instructions to compensate for detected errors and provide fault tolerance. The assertions can be applied to all the data types available in the languages. Executable assertions can also be used in a proof of correctness. This paper describes the syntax of the assertions, which contain first-order logical expressions. Examples are given of their use in a simple but practical example, the calculation of the time that a ballistic projectile travels.

articleTitle: Analysis Time, Accuracy And Memory Requirement Tradeoffs In Spice2
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: SPICE2 has proven to be an effective electronic circuit simulation program. Nonetheless, needs exist for faster computational performance and the ability to simulate economically larger circuits, especially large MOS circuits. Tradeoffs are necessary between accuracy and memory with circuit size and between accuracy and computational speed. For a bench mark example of a binary-to-octal decoder, the above aspects are illustrated. In addition, computational time that is required for different levels of device models is illustrated together with the savings achieved using a device bypass scheme and table lookup models.

articleTitle: Multidimensional Oriented Discrete Systems--characterization And Realization
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A novel class of multidimensional systems, called oriented discrete systems, is defined and character- ized. This class includes those multidimensional systems which have been called "causal", but it is much broader. It represents the practical, rather than analytical, generalization of I-D causal systems to multidimensions. The realization problem for oriented discrete systems is introduced, and in characterizing these systems, the notions of causality and recursibility for multidimensional systems are also discussed.

articleTitle: Rationalized Hadamard-haar Transform
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A hybrid version of Haar (HT) and Walsh-Hadamard transforms (WHT) called Hadamard-Haar trans form (HHT)r which effectively combines the advantages of both the transforms has been developed. Recently HT has beet rationalized such that the Powers of Y'2 are replaced by integer powers of 2 [11-131. Besides, the rationalized HT (RHT) retains all the properties of HT. Similar to (RHT), the (HHT)r 'IS now rationalized. Fast algorithms for efficient implementation of rationalized HHT (RHHT)r based on sparse matrix factors are now developed. Also by using pipeline structure, realrtime digital processors are now designed. These hardware utilize only adders, subtractors and delay units.

articleTitle: Initial Design Considerations For A Hierarchical Ic Design System
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: This paper describes the initial design of a comprehensive hierarchical intergrated circuit design system, that is currently being implemented at Stanford University. This system encourages the use of structured hardware design techniques. It is intended for the design and layout of large-scale integrated circuits by means of a combination of manual and algorithmic techniques.

articleTitle: Integrated Input Circuits For Photo Detectors
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: The input circuit associated with an integrated photo diode array has to satisfy several requirements: 1. To assure constant bias voltage for a given diode with varying illumination, the ac input impedance of the circuit should be low; 2. To assure approximately the same bias voltage for each diode in the circuit, the bias should be independent of the physical properties (threshold voltage, etc.) of the input device; 3. For compact and inexpensive realization, the circuit must be simple, and suitable for realization as a MOS integrated circuit. The paper discusses several circuits which satisfy these requirements. All rely on the closely matched properties of MOS devices which are located adjacently to each other and, in some cases, share their electrodes. Some of these circuits have been built as MOS integrated circuits, and the calculated behavior successfully verified. In the paper, the physical principles of the circuits are described, along with a simpli fied analysis based on the square-law formula for the saturation currents of all MOSFET devices. Computer-aided analysis, and subsequent bench tests performed on the realized circuits, corroborated the validity of the approximations made.

articleTitle: Frequency Domain Adaptive Correlator
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A specific configuration of an adaptive process, called a Frequency Domain Adaptive Correlator, is analyzed and simulated. The processor is used to de tect narrowband signals in broadband noise. The pro- cessor is shown to be slightly superior to conventional processors under ideal noise conditions, and signifi- cantly superior for practical noise conditions.

articleTitle: Multiple Coherence
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Microwave Lumped-element Vco And Multichip Power Combiners
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: Varactor Tuned Gunn oscillators and chip-level IMPATT diode power combiners have been fabricated at frequen cies as high as 12 GHz using lumped element circuits. Techniques for the design and fabrication of such circuits have been developed and their advantages investigated. The best lumped-element VCO tuned from 6 to 11.3 GHz with no evidence of spurious outputs. A six-mesa series-parallel array of GaAs IMPATT diode chips generated 22.5 watts CW with 20.5% efficiency at 8.65 GHz.

articleTitle: A Fast Algorithm For Space Variant Contrast Stretching
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: The operation of convolution (for the purpose of edge enhancement) can be decomposed into two terms, one of which varies quite slowly over the image being filtered. By the use of two dimensional interpolation, this spatial redundancy may be exploited in order to achieve a fast two dimensional convolution procedure for a particular class of operators. Viewed in this sense, conventional (linear) edge enhancement may be interpreted as a dynamic shifting of the "local mean". A space variant contrast stretch <1,2,3> may then be seen as a non-linear procedure in which both the local mean and the local standard deviation of an image are dynamically shifted. The same fast algorittm may then be applied to the nonlinear space variant case.

articleTitle: Generation Of 3-sigma Circuit Models And Its Applicaton To Statistical Worst-case Analysis Of Integrated Circuit Designs
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: Introduced in this paper is the concept of statistical worst-case, circuit design based on simulation using the 3-sigma circuit models. Here, the 3-sigma model is defined as a model, which, if being utilized for circuit analysis, will simulate the performance of a circuit design which is 3-sigma away from the nominal characteristics. For illustrations, the 3-sigma circuit models of an ECL circuit design are derived via the solution of quadratic programming.

articleTitle: A Mask Pattern Analyzer With Circuit Check Data And Logic Simulation Outputs
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A mask pattern analyzer is described which features pattern generator tape and node overlay inputs and generates [1[ a floating node report t [2] floating branch report [3] a LOOCAP direct network file and [4] a LOGCAP with review file. All standard NAND, NOR, AND-OR-INVERT, OR-AND- INVERT circuits and nearly all transmission gate logic elements are synthesized directly into LOGCAP defined devices and placed in the LOGCAP network file. Circuits for which non-standard configurations are synthesized are placed in a file for review to make sure the logic synthesized is intended and not the result of errors in the layout or the node overlay. The analyzer also features an option allowing the user to direct the formation of subnets through the node overlay. Mirroring and/or rotation of previously defined subnets in the node overlay is permitted. When the subnet options are invoked, a subnet stringlist is generated as a 5th report.

articleTitle: Broadcast Channels With And Without Feedback
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Stability Diagram For An Adaptive Recursive Filter
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: A Comparison Of Some Subjective And Objective Measures For Image Quality
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Salsim - A Language For Control Of Digital Logic Simulation
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: SALOGS is the logic simulation code normally used as the first step in design of large scale logic arrays. SALOGS contains a simulation control language called SALSIM which permits structured programs to be written to apply inputs to a network, control printing and control program execution. This paper discusses the SALSIM language.

articleTitle: A Study Of Third-order Intermodulation Distortion Product's Of GaAs Power Fets
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: In this paper the 4 GHz tnird-order intermodulation disto-rtion behavior of fouf power GaAs FETs from three manufactures is studiej. Two-tone IMD data is given for each device for three tuning conditions: best smail-signal gain, best large-signal gain, and a compromise between gain and better IMD behavior. The ImD was not "well-behaved" in ganerai (3:1 IIAD slope), but rather went irregularly as 4:1 to 6:1. Some degree of gain expansion was observed with each (Device. Since the thiru order IMD products '30 not rise steadily at 3:1, the third-order intercept point is not valij in describing these devices. The I dB gain compression point is poorly defined in cases where there is gain -expansion.

articleTitle: Stability Conditions For Multidimensional Filters
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Dynamic Allocation Of Arrays In Fortran
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: An operational mechanism is discussed for the dynamic allocation/deallocation of Fortran arrays. Implementation is possible on any computer which allows dynamic memory allocation at the assembly language level. The crux of the technique is a protocol for accessing dynamically allocated memory from Fortran in a natural manner.

articleTitle: Linear Processing Of Nonuniformly Sampled Signals: A Fourier Analysis
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: The concept of frequency transfer function plays a fundamental role in characterizing a linear digital signal processor's dynamical behavior. Invariably, the input number sequence to be operated upon is assumed to have originated through the process of uniformly sampling a continuous-time signal. It is then only natural that most studies related to a linear digital signal processor's transfer function are based upon the uniform sampling model. In a variety of very important applications, however, the number sequence to be pro cessed is generated by a nonuniform sampling scheme. For example, in radar signal processing, stagger sampling is often used in order to reduce the effects of the Sampled Signals so-called "blind velocity"phenomenon (e.g., see refs.

articleTitle: Power GaAs Fet Amplifier Design With Large Signal Tuning Parameters
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: The large-signal tuning parameters have been measured for three medium power GaAs FETs in both chip and packaged form. The output tuning parameter ( rL) is especially important for determining the output power, gain, and efficiency of power GaAs FET amplifiers. The effect of detuning from the optimum point has been measured. The application of large signal tuning parameters to a 4-8 GHz power amplifier design is included.

articleTitle: A New Look At Broad-banding
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A new approach for broad-band matching on arbi- trary load to a resistive generator leads to a simple technique for the design of a lossless 2-port equalizer, The method utilizes real frequency impedance data, bypassing analytic gain-bandwidth theory. Neither the equalizer topology nor the analytic form of the system transfer function are assumed. These result from the design process. Various examples which demonstrate the flexibility of the method are presented. Finally a practical microwave FET amplifier design is given.

articleTitle: An Electrical Surge Arrestor (ESA) Model For Computer-aided Design And Evaluation
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: Electrical Surge Arrestors (ESA's) are widely used to protect susceptible electrical and electronic components sub-systems and systems from the potentially damaging (usually in nano henries) effects of lightning, static discharge, Electromagnetic interference and the Electromagnetic pulse arising from associated with L (usually in potential nuclear weapon detonations. ESA's are very non- linear devices when operating near or above the DC break down potential. The ESA model to be described accounts (reflected capacitance at the for a significant number of nonlinear effects including (1) all other sources, leads, streamer formation, (2) plasma conductivity, (3) glow region, (4) arc extinguishing, (5) high frequency oscilla tions, (6) Thermionic effects, and (7) heating and heat (measured or calculated for dissipation to the surrounding medium. The model is illus- trated in Figure I with a corresponding definition for each parameter in the model.

articleTitle: Adaptive Transfer Filter Considerations
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A novel filter configuration known as the adaptive transfer filter is introduced. The performance of this filter is compared emperically with the conventional filter configuration which is generally referred to as the adaptive noise-cancellation filter. In the related experiments, both filters are implemented via Widrow's LMS (least-mean-square) algorithm.

articleTitle: Data Flow Implementation Of Two Dimensional Recursive Digital Filters
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Optimum Data Quantization For A General Signal Detection Problem
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: On The Implementation Of A 2-d Fir Filter Using A Single Multiplier
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: Rabiner and Goldl have outlined an approach to the implementation of one-dimensional FIR digital filters using only one multiplier. This direct implemen- tation uses shift registers to store input values and either shift registers or read-only-memories (ROM's) to store the filter coefficients. Through appropriate shifting, the correct input and filter coefficient pair are presented to the multiplier inputs. These products are accumulated by an adder and a storage register. The main advantage of this technique is that only one multiplier is needed regardless of filter order thus reducing cost and power requirements.

articleTitle: Representation Of Continuous-time State Equations By Discrete-time State Equations
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A method, based on multi-feedback and multi-feedforward control theory, is developed in the time domain for accurately representing continuous-time state equations by discrete-time state equations. A matrix continued fraction method is used as a basis for this work. It is shown that several commonly used con version procedures are special cases of the method proposed in this paper. It is also shown that if a more accurate model is developed, a larger sampling period can be used. The relaxation of the sampling period requirement facill tates the practical implementation of systems.

articleTitle: Ion Implanted GaAs Fet Devices And Circuits
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Device-circuit Considerations In The Design Of Broadband Mesfet Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: The Design Of A 10 Mhz To 2.5 Ghz Mesfet Amplifier Is Discussed. Comparisons Are Made Of Circuit Considerations And Their Relations To Device Parameters For Amplifiers With And Without Feedback. A Significant Requirement Of The Amplifier Was Low Distor Tion At Output Levels Of Greater Than 16 Dbm. The Consi.derations Involved In Such A Design Are Also Discussed, And The Performance Of Two Such Amplifiers Given.

articleTitle: Design Of High Power C-band GaAs Fet Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: Design procedures for FET power amplifiers are described and ex perimental results obtained in a five-stage C-band amplifier are presented as an example. The amplifier was designed for a power output of I watt in the 4.4-5.0 GHz band with a linear gain of 50 dB.

articleTitle: Miniature Image Reject Mixers And Their Use In Low-noise Front-ends In Conjunction With Gaas Fet Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: It is shown that the Image Reject Mixer (IRM) resistively terminates the image sideband by downconverting it to an out put port that is physically distinct from the I port. The Image Reject Mixer is also shown to be a dual channel downconverter that downconverts the upper sideband and lower sideband to two distinct I ports and, consequently this IRM is the ideal mixer to be used after an RF amplifier. It is also shown that the image sideband does not have to be reactively terminated in a recovery type low noise IRM.

articleTitle: Viterbi Algorithm Receivers For Nonlinear Satellite Channels
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Statistical Characterization Of Intermittent Faults In Digital Systems
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Image Alignment Through Information Content
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: A High Performance Microprocessor-based Digital Controller
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: In recent years a trend toward the use of microprocessors for controlling high performance analog servosystems has developed. This paper dis cusses such an application, to a military system, the power drives of the NAVY GFCS Director MK68. The MK68 is a shipboard device designed to fac iliate the directing of various weapons hardware, such as gun mounts and rocket launchers, by maintaining radar and optical line-of-slight to targets, and providing bearing and elevation information to the fire control computer.

articleTitle: Optimal Weighting Functions For Cross Correlation Of Distorted Images
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: The detection performance of the two-dimensional cross correlation algorithm applied to two images with relative geometric distortion is presented. The per- formance measure used is the peak-to-sidelobe ratio. The geometric distortion is modeled by an affine transformation of image coordinates. The spatial window function applied to one of the images before cross correlation with the other one is optimized for a given distortion. The expression for peak-to-sidelobe is shown to be maximized by the window function.

articleTitle: An Improved Successive-approximation Register Design For Use In Monolithic A/D Converters
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: An improved design for a successive-approximation register (SAR) for use in A/D converters is presented. The proposed design is suitable for 12L imple mentation such that a definite savings in devices is obtained over previous designs using the separate sequencer and code register approach. This par ticular design scheme operates in a fully synchro-nous mode with the clock allowing a reduction in propagation delay to be realized.

articleTitle: "Active Realization Of A Negative Inductor"
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A generalized expression defining the input admittance of any single op.amp. active-RC network is formulated. It is used to synthesize an ideal negative inductor using only one capacitor and two resistors. Due to practical limitations, the quality' factor of the inductor is finite, but high. Also, an extra resistor has to be added to the network. However, the Q-factor can be made infinite at any one specific frequency.

articleTitle: Universal To Device Controller By Using Programmable Logic Arrays (pla)
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A flexible IO device controller architecture with a PLA and a microprocessor is introduced. By use of the CPU interface control, great flexibility to various CPU interfaces can be achieved. Applicability to many kinds of device controllers and capability to extend functions are also achieved under microprogrammed control. The implementation of this architecture to a disk con troller shows the reduction of packaging area to 1/3 of that of the conventional hardwired controller.

articleTitle: Design Of Tracking Filters
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: This paper outlines the design of tracking filters. Such high-Q band-pass filters achieve good signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) and track wandering carrier frequencies to maintain the same SNR. An actual tracking filter is specified, designed, implemented, and tested.

articleTitle: Adaptive Noise Cancelling Via Input Equalization
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: An Approach To The Design Of Decoupled Systems In The Presence Of Large Parameter Variations
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: In this study we outline a design approach for decoupled control systems in the presence of large parameter variations. The decoupling problem is of practical interest in flight control problems, especially in the landing mode where it is desireable to independently control certain output variables, e.g., flight path angle, forward speed, etc. A common source of parameter variations in fliaht control Droblems is the result of linear ization about a n@mber of difierent operating points. It is assumed in this study that parameter variations may be represented by a discrete finite set of possible values, corresponding to different flight conditions and that the complete system state is not available.

articleTitle: Calculation Of Prolate Spheroidal Functions For Use In Finite Fourier Transform Operations
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Initial Condition Calculation
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A method is presented for the calculation of the initial values of the dependent variables and their derivatives when the network equations are mixed differential-algebraic and implicit in the derivatives. That is, it calculates values for W(O) and W(O) for systems of equations in the form q(W,W,t) = 0. The crux of the problem can be revealed as follows: Equations in the above form do not reveal a dynamically independent set of variables. Even if a set is known and initial values are assigned to them, there sti II remains the need to cal cu I ate the i ni ti al values for the remaining variables and for the derivatives of all the variables. This is true even for derivatives that do not appear in the network equations since knowledge of their values simplifies integration of the network equations by a predictor-corrector scheme. The method presented allows initial conditions to be speci fied by a system of equations of the form p(W(O) W(O) 0. ( This corresponds to speci fyi ng the v a I ue,s of the dyn am ic variables in some other methods). If the number of arbitrary initial conditions allowable by q is greater than specified by p, the method will set a sufficient number of elements of W and/or W to zero.

articleTitle: Input Matching: A New Procedure For Adaptive Control Design
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: Adaptive input matching, based on directly adapt- ing controller parameters to form a control effort matching a desired input, bypasses the identifiability constraints of indirect adaptive control and the per- fect matching limitations of current direct adaptive exact output/model matching schemes. This original concept allows combination of stable parameter adjust ment algorithms and optimal performance considerations. Furthermore, the focus on input matchability allows consistent control despite inconsistent control parame- ter identification. Examination of three diverse plant objective classes demonstrates the immediate broad ap- plicability of the input matching concept and provides several suggestions for further application of this new procedure for adaptive control design.

articleTitle: Topological Evaluation Of The Null Return Difference In Feedback Amplifier Theory
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: Like the general return difference, the general null return difference is defined as the ratio of the two functional values assumed by the second-order cofactor of the elements as sociated with the input and output terminals of the indefinite-admittance matrix of a feed back amplifier under the condition that the element of interest assumes its nominal value and the condition that the element assumes its reference value, It is shown that this alge braic definition is entirely consistent with the classical physical formulation of the null return difference. Topological formulas are presented for the null return difference and the sensitivity functions in terms of the directed-tree and directed-two-tree products in the associated digraph of the amplifier.

articleTitle: Hamiltonian Rectangular Lattices
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Animal Biotemetry Studies Historical Perspectives And Recent Applications
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Amplifier Design Considerations
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Adaptive Identification Of And Pole Placement For Stable Plants
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: The improved parameter identification and state observation technique of a recent paper by to adaptively place the poles of an nth order single-output, linear time-invariant stable system having unknown parameters to arbitrarily specified locations in the open left half-plane. The proposed scheme uses only input and output measureme- ments, has an arbitrarily fast exponential conver- gence and is totally stable.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuits For Impatt And Other Microwave Diodes
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: Equivalent circuits for active semiconductor devices are useful for designing oscillators and amplifiers. However, the parameters are unlikely to represent physical elements of the device. Parameters of passive devices are more easily related to specific portions of the device, although it is not necessary that this equivalence hold true. Package and mount impedances further complicate this problem.

articleTitle: Toward A Methodology For Model-sensitivity Analysis
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: In addition to the work on sensitivity analysis in the control theory literature, other methods and concepts have arisen in general modeling and in chemical kinetics modeling. In an attempt to reconcile different viewpoints and perspectives a preliminary methodology for model-sensitivity is presented. It involves concepts describing the domain of uncertainty, the measure of sensitivity, separability, and computational costs. The characteristic of separability is especially important in methods used for the repeated study of the same model.

articleTitle: Modeling And Identification Of Fluid Dynamic Phenomena For Slender Bodies
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: This paper surveys the fluid dynamic effects which significantly affect the forces and moments acting on an appended slender body of revolution. The goal is to determine a model structure suitable for use in a maximum likelihood system identification algorithm. Fluid phenomena considered are linear effects modeled by potential flow theory and the nonlinear effects of leeside vortices, free vortices, and the Magnus effect. Particular emphasis is placed on the determin- ation of which effects involve memory (thus increasing the order of the system) and the isolation of those dimensionless parameters which cannot be determined with consistency from current fluid mechanics theory. Applications are to submersible ocean-going vehicles and to missiles.

articleTitle: Multiprocessing With The Ti 9900
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: Increased data rates and accuracies have caused needs for increased computational power to process data at remote sites. multiprocessing with microprocessors is one solution to the processing problem. The processing approach calls for subdivid ing the processing into separate tasks, each of which are assigned to a processor for execution. The multiprocessor architecture consists of a Main Memory for data buffering, Processors as needed by the problem solution, and Local Memories for each processor. A modular approach to the hardware design utilizing shared buses is presented.

articleTitle: Cryptographic Protection Of Information In Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Recursive Restoration Of Astigmatism
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A new adaptive recursive approach based on a state space model is introduced for restoring images degraded by astigmatism. The technique is very attractive in light of computational considerations and yields exact restoration in the absence of random noise. In addition, the recursive nature of the approach makes it well suited to computer implementation.

articleTitle: Equivalent Gain Forms For CTD Filters
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: There are three equivalent forms for expressing the gains of transversal analog filters which are mechanized with charge-transfer devices (CTD's) Due to charge-transfer inefficiency (CTI), q, the equivalence of expression is not obvious. This paper presents a simple tabulation of equivalences, their uses, and their derivations. This problem and solution also extend to include the recursive case. Arbitrary discrete-time recursive transfer functions are often mechanized digitally as second-order sections. Equivalent analog realization using charge-transfer devices can not use the same gain parameters becuase of the effects (again) of charge transfer inefficiency. This paper further includes an expression for corrected gains to compensate for this charge-transfer inefficiency in the recursive structure.

articleTitle: Waveform Analysis Using Zero-detection With Applications To Speech Processing
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: On Error Clustering In Digital Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Stochastic Analysis Of Iterative Image Reconstruction Algorithms
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: A Class Of Oscillators With Independently Adjustable Frequency, Amplitude, And Transient Response
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A class of third order harmonic oscillators with frequency, amplitude, and transient response controlled by three separate sets of parameters is derived. A simplified oscillator is described in which there are only three parameters, one which controls the frequency, another the amplitude, and the third the transient response. The oscillator contains a single nonlinearity, which can be either of the saturation or the dead space type. The mathematical analysis is based on linearizing the nonlinearity by means of the sinusoidal describing func tion. The transient response is studied by considering small amplitude perturba tions away from the oscillator's limit cycle. The results of analog computer simulations are presented with emphasis on the relationship between transient response and the gain controlling it.

articleTitle: A Graphical Stability Test Of Two-dimensional Multi-input Multi-output Digital Filters
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Structured Programming And Software Engineering Of Hard-real-time Minicomputer Systems
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: This paper describes a structured approach to the development and implementation of real-time minicomputer software systems. The method adapts sound, proved engineer ing techniques into software project engineering terms. These software engineering practices presume technical expertise as a necessity, but also utilize top-down design and implementation principles, structured programming concepts, concurrent documenta tion and implementation activities, management visibility and control mechanisms, soft ware standards, and coordinated project teamwork.

articleTitle: A Security Analysis Of The Federal Data Encryption Standard
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: Modifications increasing the cryptanalysis resitance of the National Bureau of Standards developed Federal Data Encryption Standard are discussed.

articleTitle: New Techniques For Active Filter Design Incorporating Modern Operational Amplifier Technologies
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A straightforward approach to active filter amplifier design is presented, where by highly stabilized, wide band operational amplifiers are used in positive feed back configurations as low-gain isolation elements between cascaded single pole R-C networks. Modern BiFET amplifiers operating in the near unity gain mode having bandwidths ranging from 5 to 15 MHz may be used in bandpass configurations with center frequencies out to approximately half the amplifier bandwidth with the amplifiers treated as ideal gain elements and to near the bandwidth limit if the amplifier poles are incorporated into the response function.

articleTitle: Frequency-wavenumber Processing Of Unequally Spaced Line Arrays
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Sanctuary Signal Processing Requirements
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Optimal Tracking Of A Markov Jump Process
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A feedback control is obtained for a linear random tracking problem with a quadratic performance measure. Both inputs to the system and the reference vector, which is to be tracked, are capable of instantaneous change.

articleTitle: A New Algorithm For Plotting Root LOCI (With Applications)
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: The position of a root on the s-plane depends on the characteristic equation and is a ans function of the 'root locus' gain. Using small perturbations and expanding in a Tay lor's series a simple algorithm is obtained which permits calculation of the root locus without factoring the polynomial.

articleTitle: Maximum Firing Number In Capacitated Marked Graphs
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: The maximum number of times that a vertex x can be fired in a capac itated marked graph is called the maximum firing number of x. This paper shows that the maximum firing number p(x) of a vertex x is equal to the minimum "distance" from x to a vertex z such that P(Z) = 0.

articleTitle: A New State-variable Formulation Of Network Equations For Linear Networks
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: This paper presents a new state-variable formulation of network function for a general linear network. Three distinguished features of the formu lation are: (i) Using node formulation as basis, it requires less memory space than the conventional state-variable formulation [1]. (ii) It in cludes the dependent source as an element whose transfer ratio can be a function of s.(iii) Its speed is fast for networks with no inductors. With these three features, it is a useful and powerful tool for analyzing practical linear integrated circuits in the s-domain.

articleTitle: Optimal Inputs For Blood Glucose Regulation Parameter Estimation
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: The estimation of the parameters for blood glucose regulation can be enhanced by using a glucose infusion input which is optimal in some mathematical sense. Using a linear two-compartment model, techniques are given for deriving the optimal input. Methods of extending the techniques for different performance criteria and more complex glucose regu- lation models are discussed. The results may eventually prove useful for developing new clinical tests which can differentiate the normal patient from the diabetic.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Forecasting Algorithm
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: The forecasting of discrete-time random processes with nonstationary statistics has long been recognized as an important problem [1,21. In particular, inventory control in e.g. retail stores with a large variety of items relies on the manager's ability to forecast future demands based on periodically spaced ac- counts of the actual demand which themselves show wide variation. Many forecasting algorithms have been presented in the literature [1-41. The varying degrees of complexity depend to a great extent on the model used for the demand process. One popular assumption on the demand history for items held in inventory is that the underlying process is a continuous, piecewise linear process, i.e. reflecting trend changes in de- mand. Perhaps, a more realistic model would allow for inaccuracies and complexities of the actual demand process by including the effects of both correlated and uncorrelated errors in the measured sequence of demand data. With this background the next section presents a reasonable stochastic model for the demand process and an explicit statement of the estimation problem to be investigated in this paper.

articleTitle: Design Of An Infrared Sensor To Estimate Target Parameters
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: "Investigation Of The Coupling In The Single Tuned Waveguide Coaxial Oscillator"
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: The two resonance behavior of this basic circuit is discussed. It was found that input coupling coefficient was an especially important factor in the behavior of the input im pedance loci. This coupling was then studied with the intent of determining its functional dependance on physical dimensions and circuit Q. A modification of the first theory was required in order to get qualitative agreement with measured results.

articleTitle: Application Of Ispice To Worst Case Circuit Design And Analysis
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: The interest of the discrete circuit designer usually lies in the area of tolerance assignment and cumulative impact of component variation. The integrated device designer requires the impact of processing related parameters on many elements in some consistent fashion. The convenience and completeness of treating both requirements with ISPICE is described.

articleTitle: Lumped Model For Single Silicon Beam Filters
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A linearized lumped model is presented for resonant beams etched from Silicon. From this, the deflection, for small motions, versus input voltage is determined. Discussion is given on the use for filter transfer function calculation and extensions to multibeaja structures.

articleTitle: A Linearized Transient Analysis Method For Computing Frequency Response In Circuit Simulators
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A new method for computing electronic circuit small-signal frequency response is introduced. This method, when implemented in a circuit simulator that has a transient analysis capability, requires minimal additional memory and software. Because complex arithmetic is not required, this method is particularly suited to minicomputer simulators. The frequency response of both linear and nonlinear circuits is possible. The frequency response of high-Q circuits, although more time consuming, is also possible. Magnitude and phase errors of less than 1% and 0.5 degrees, respectively, are easily attainable. Speed ratios between this method and a conventional ac analysis vary depending on the circuit Q. For circuits with Q less than 1, this ratio is typically 10:1.

articleTitle: A Charge-oriented Model For MOS Transistor Capacitances
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A new model for computer simulation of capacitance effects in MOS transistors is presented. Transient currents are found directly from the charge distribu- tion in the device rather than from capacitances. The effective capacitances which result are non-reciprocal. The model guarantees conservation of charge and includes bulk capacitances. Several circuit examples are considered.

articleTitle: Examples Of Maximum Likelihood Spatial Filtering
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Rational Analysis Of Nonuniform Distributed Networks
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A set of arrarys as well as its algorithm and the generating procedure are presented for the appro- ximative formulation of rational polynomials of a rion- uniform distributed network. It greatly simplifies and also generalizes the entire calculation procedure.

articleTitle: Finite Elements For Semiconductor Device Simulation
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A two-dimensional formulation of the finite-element method for semiconductor devices is described which is current conservative irrespective of the choice of element functions. An implementation is outlined which includes Gummel's algorithm for potential calculation and an adaptation of Sharfetter's method for current calculation. Results for a charge coupled device and a one-dimensional p-n junction diode are given and compared with finite difference calculations. An example is also given for an SOS device.

articleTitle: Automatic Digital Audio Processor (adap)
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Schematic Logic - A Software Design Notation
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: Pseudocode and flowcharts are the two most popular notational aids currently used while performing program design. A third notation, schematic logic, is introduced and demonstrated. Advantages of schematic logic are: it is easy to use, it encourages stepwise refinement, it records success levels of conceptual ization, and it helps verify solution completeness.

articleTitle: Ladder Forms Lin Estimation And System Identification
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Architecture For Contekporary Computer Aids To Geverate Ic Mask Layouts
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: A new automatic IC mask layout code, SICLOPS is being developed which avoids most of the problems inherent in the present generation of layout codes such as lack of flexibilityy inefficient use of area, and restricted design complexity. The basic architecture, philosophy, and assumptions used in developing the code are described.

articleTitle: The Design Of Digital Single-sideband Modulators Using A Multirate Digital Filter
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.

articleTitle: Hardware-software Tradeoffs In Reliable Software Development
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: Advances in computer technology are offering opportunities for innovative hardware-software tradeoffs for reducing system development costs and improving software reliability and performance. However, some project managers are not yet taking full advantage of these opportunities. They tend to proceed immediately to hardware specification and acquisition, and only later turn to software planning and design. The likely outcome is cost and schedule overruns, inefficient software structures, inadequate performance, and poor soft- ware reliability. An approach more apt to produce satisfactory results is to generate hardware and software specifications together as a synergistic whole, and then acquire the two as balanced and compatible parts of the system's architecture. This paper addresses hardware-software tradeoff oppor- tunities, computer tools for tradeoff analyses, and a management approach.

articleTitle: Analytical And Experimental Analysis Of Routing Algorithms
publicationTitle: 1977 11th Asilomar Conference on Circuits, Systems and Computers, 1977. Conference Record.
abstract: Experiments to compare the performance of several widely-used interconnection routing algorithms are described. Examples of the experimental results are given and their implications discussed.
